title: Nontraditional Talent Pipeline & Skills Validation Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for creating a complementary hiring lane for nontraditional candidates (bootcamps, career-changers, senior ICs from adjacent domains). The focus: fast, fair signal -> validated readiness -> low-friction onboard. Goal is to reduce time-to-offer for viable candidates while increasing diversity of background and keeping ramp outcomes predictable.

High-level objectives (what success looks like):
- 30% of hires in the pilot cohort come from nontraditional channels (next 6 months).
- Offer-to-accept conversion >= 70% for validated candidates.
- 60-day competency signal: 80% of hires hitting core role checkpoint.
- Reduce recruiter time-per-qualified by 20% via standardized micro-projects and auto-eval rubric.

Scope & constraints:
- Roles in scope initially: Platform SRE, Backend Engineer II, Applied ML Engineer (inference-focused), Solutions Engineer.
- Not in scope: Senior manager hires, sensitive security-clearance roles, roles requiring >5y domain-specific regulatory experience.
- Pilot size: 8 hires over 3 months.

Pipeline stages (proposed flow):
1) Sourcing: partner bootcamps + community events + targeted LinkedIn + internal referrals. Tag candidates with source.
2) Quick screen (30m) with recruiter: culture fit, logistics, salary band. Use standard recruiter checklist (see TODO template).
3) Micro-project invite (take-home, 72h) -> standardized evaluation rubric. Projects are role-focused, scaffolded, and low-cost to evaluate.
4) Pairing interview (60m): technical deep dive based on micro-project outputs, emphasis on design and tradeoffs.
5) System fit / team interview (45m): cross-collaboration scenarios.
6) Offer + role-specific ramp plan (30/60/90) and mentor assignment.

Micro-project design principles:
- 4–6 hour implementation surface, can be completed with pseudocode for some parts.
- Clear acceptance criteria and sample test cases.
- Must reveal: problem decomposition, tradeoffs, testability, and ability to communicate unknowns.
- Scoring: 6 categories (correctness, design, clarity, tests, performance considerations, tradeoffs) 1-5 each. Threshold to progress: average >=3.2 and no category <2.
- Fast grader option: structured checklist so non-technical recruiters can do a first pass (yes/no flags) before engineering graders.

Interview rubric (pair interview + system fit) — condensed (for interviewer cheat-sheet):
- Problem framing (10%): did candidate restate constraints, ask clarifying q's?
- Depth of design (35%): component choices, APIs, failure modes, monitoring + SLO awareness (for infra roles).
- Implementation reasoning (25%): ability to reason about complexity and edge cases; read code submitted in micro-project.
- Communication & collaboration (15%): explains tradeoffs and alternatives; seeks feedback.
- Learning mindset & growth signals (15%): examples of adapting to unfamiliar tech and rapid learning.
Scoring guidance: numeric 1-5 per axis + brief comment. Put scores into JIRA-HIRE-312.

Onboarding checklist (first 30 days — role-agnostic template):
Pre-Start (HR/IT):
- Contract + equity docs signed, payroll setup, benefits enrollment link shared.
- Machines ordered + OS image request -> use infra-onboard-sprint template.
- Access: Okta invite, Slack, Google Drive group, Jira projects, Github org read access.
Day 0–3:
- Welcome call with people ops and hiring manager.
- 2hr product + infra overview recorded session.
- Env setup: repo clone, local dev runbook, smoke test.
- Assign mentor and first-week paired work: small bugfix or doc update.
Week 1 deliverables:
- Complete micro-project postmortem: document what they learned, what they'd change.
- Setup monitoring/alerting sandbox (infra roles) or run end-to-end quick demo (app roles).
- 1:1 scheduling cadence agreed with manager and mentor.
30-day checkpoint (manager):
- Core competency checklist review: role-specific signals (list attached in appendices).
- Identify two stretch tasks and a concrete 60-day learning plan.

Mentor rotation and expectations:
- Mentor rotation: mentors rotate every 4–6 weeks in the pilot (shadow, then lead). Purpose: cross-team exposure, accelerate context sharing, and reduce single-point-of-failure.
- Mentor duties (first 30 days): daily check-ins first week, pair on first deliverable, unblock infra/code access, first performance feedback.
- Mentor evaluation: short pulse in week 3 (template in linked artifacts).

Acceptance & risk signals (for go/no-go at 30 days):
- Positive signals: shipped a small, reviewable change; documented system context; able to navigate build and test pipeline without help.
- Risk signals (escalate): repeated blocker on basic infra access after 48h; inability to explain micro-project tradeoffs; team collaboration red flags (missed paired sessions with no notice).

Compensation & offer mechanics (pilot):
- Target bands will follow existing role bands; for nontraditional candidates we can include a $5k learning stipend for first 6 weeks to cover tooling/courseing if necessary. Must be approved per REQ.
- Standard signoff: hiring manager + people-ops + finance. Use JIRA-HIRE-312 for approvals.

Operational playbooks & templates to build (TODO list):
- Micro-project library (5 per role) + auto-checker where feasible.
- Recruiter quick-check grading sheet.
- Interviewer one-page rubric PDF.
- 30/60/90 ramp templates per role.
- Mentor rotation schedule template and mentor pulse form.
- Candidate FAQ doc: pay bands, remote policy, relocation, visa.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Leveling: how strictly do we map micro-project outcomes to level? (default: pass -> level as defined by hiring manager; see CONFLUENCE-6791).
- Pay band adjustments for career-changers with limited domain history.
- Legal review on stipend wording for contractors vs employees.

Quick list of sample micro-project prompts (short):
- Infra: Add a caching layer to reduce N+1 calls on a small API; measure expected latency improvement.
- Backend: Implement pagination and idempotent retry logic for a batch endpoint; include tests.
- Applied ML (inference): Build a tiny transformer inference pipeline wrapper that supports batching and returns latency metrics (can be pseudocode).
- Solutions Eng: Draft a 15-minute customer troubleshooting playbook for "service degradation" scenario and a small sample diagnostic script.

Notes to self / meeting trail:
- Discuss with Marco (sourcing) 2025-11-09 — agreed to trial two bootcamp partners.
- Ling to draft micro-project templates by 2025-11-20.
- Rory to validate stipend legal language with finance (ticket FIN-88).

Appendix: sample 30-day competency checklist (short):
- Can run local dev environment end-to-end.
- Completed first code review and responded to feedback.
- Demonstrated basic ownership of an assigned bug/feature.
- Knows who to escalate infra incidents to.

This doc is intentionally a working draft: expect edits, link additions, and a first in-person sync with hiring managers on 2025-11-16.

Unresolved tags / follow-ups: 
- Add anonymized micro-project examples for public sharing.
- Create dashboard to track pilot metrics (sourcing -> offer -> 60-day competency).
